edges.label: Authored the Air Force's report to the Secretary and GAO
edges.note: Written by Col. Weaver, Director of Security and Special Program Oversight, Office of the Secretary of the Air Force, with 1st Lt. James McAndrew.

edges.label: Marcel physically handled the recovered debris
edges.note: The 509th's staff intelligence officer collected the Foster ranch material with CIC Capt. Sheridan Cavitt and carried it to Fort Worth. His custody role is documented in the Air Force's own 1995 report.

edges.label: The Air Force reports were produced to rebut Marcel's account
edges.note: Marcel's 1978 recantation restarted the case; the 1994-1997 Air Force volumes exist because of it and conclude against him, attributing the debris to Project MOGUL and reported bodies to test dummies.

edges.label: The AMC commander's 1947 assessment predates and undercuts the MOGUL account
edges.note: Twining wrote in September 1947 that the phenomenon was real while noting the lack of recovered exhibits; the Air Force's 1994 position requires that his own command's exploitation centre never connected the wave to a programme it was cleared for.

a.label: Plains of San Agustin, New Mexico

edges.label: alleged second recovery site (Barnett account)
edges.note: TIER 3, CONTESTED. The Plains of San Agustin entered the Roswell corpus through Grady 'Barney' Barnett's reported account, transmitted second-hand and published in Berlitz and Moore's 'The Roswell Incident' (1980). The Air Force's own 1995 records review corroborates the route the story travelled - it records that in 1978 'a UFO researcher, Stanton Friedman, met with Marcel and began investigating', and that Moore and Berlitz 'reported they interviewed a number of persons who claimed to have been present at Roswell in 1947 and professed to be either firsthand or secondhand witnesses'. It does not corroborate the site: 'San Agustin', 'Barnett' and 'Maltais' each appear zero times in the entire report. Kevin Randle, named in that review among the researchers, concludes on the evidence: 'It is for these reasons, that is the lack of first-hand corroboration of the Barnett tale, the inability of the first people to talk of what Barnett said to provide a location and date and that the only source of the information is Barnett that I say, with confidence, that nothing happened there in July 1947.' Roswell is July 1947, so that conclusion severs the link by dating rather than by geography.

edges.label: MOGUL is the load-bearing element of the official explanation
edges.note: The Air Force concluded the most likely source of the recovered wreckage was a Project MOGUL balloon train, replacing the weather balloon account it had maintained since 1947.

edges.label: The press release is the event's only uncontested artifact
edges.note: Every subsequent official position — weather balloon, MOGUL, dummies — is a response to this single document issued by an atomic bomb group's own information office.

edges.label: Ramey's headquarters overrode Marcel's base-level identification
edges.note: Marcel was photographed in Ramey's office beside balloon debris on 8 July 1947; thirty-one years later he stated the material had been substituted. The photographs are reproduced in the 1995 USAF report.

edges.label: Ramey retracted the disc announcement the same day
edges.note: The Eighth Air Force commanding general personally fronted a same-day correction identifying the debris as a weather balloon with radar reflector — the founding template for official UAP retraction.

b.label: Roswell, New Mexico and the Foster Ranch, Lincoln County

edges.label: The 509th Bomb Group at Roswell AAF was the only atomic-armed unit in the world
edges.note: The recovery, the announcement and the destroyed records all belong to a single installation with the most restrictive information discipline in the US military.

edges.label: Schiff's inquiry forced the Air Force to abandon the weather balloon story
edges.note: Both Roswell Reports state they were produced in response to Rep. Schiff's inquiry. The 1994-1995 volume conceded that the 1947 weather balloon explanation was false.

edges.label: Haut issued the 8 July 1947 press release
edges.note: As RAAF public information officer Haut issued the announcement that the 509th Bomb Group had gained possession of a disc; the release is reproduced in the Air Force's own 1995 report.
